assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hijacking the ubiquitin-proteasome system with bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues is a genuinely new pharmacological principle: degrade the target instead of inhibiting it. It opens previously undruggable proteins and has moved into late-stage clinical trials. It meets my game-changer standard of something new with real consequences, and the underlying idea is simple and elegant.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept (the first compounds date to around 2001) and developed it into drugs. Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explains molecular-glue degraders. Ciulli (VHL ligands, structure-guided design), Gray, Sakamoto and Kim are strong but the three-person limit forces a choice; I would keep the concept founders plus the mechanistic glue discovery.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of work with independent confirmation across many laboratories and several clinical programmes. Approval of a PROTAC drug is still pending, but the mechanism is firmly established and recognition looks timely.
uncertainties: Whether Handa (glue mechanism) or Ciulli (VHL and structure-based design) is the better third laureate.
Clinical outcomes of PROTACs are not yet settled, and I rely on memory for the current trial status.
Compound candidate: PROTACs and molecular glues may be better recognised as separate discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors are small-molecule-like chemistry applied to the genome: deaminase chemistry converts C to T or A to G at a single base without double-strand breaks. The tool is simple in concept, was a clear break from nuclease-based editing and is already used widely in research and clinical development. It is a game-changer with demonstrated consequences.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the work, with Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor, which required evolving a deaminase for DNA) as the first authors who did the decisive experiments. Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) were independent and near-simultaneous, which complicates priority. A Nobel committee might prefer Liu alone, or Liu together with the CRISPR-adjacent prime editing in B056.
assessment.maturity: Introduced in 2016 and 2017, with extensive independent replication and first clinical use. It is early compared with most other candidates but already strongly validated.
uncertainties: Overlap with the prime-editing candidate (B056), where Liu is also central.
Whether the Chemistry Prize should come after the 2020 CRISPR prize or wait for longer clinical follow-up.
Priority of Kondo and Nishida relative to Komor and Gaudelli.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Expanding the genetic code with orthogonal tRNA/aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase pairs lets cells incorporate designed unnatural amino acids site-specifically into proteins. This is a basic reprogramming of biochemistry that is now used in protein engineering, biophysics, biotherapeutics and enzyme design. The work is original, general and has lasting consequences.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang made the first demonstrations in E. coli and yeast and set the conceptual and technical foundation. Chin extended it to higher organisms and to quadruplet codons and orthogonal ribosomes. Mehl and Yokoyama are also credited and made real contributions, so the three-person cut is a judgement call.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of independent confirmation in many laboratories, and wide use. Recognition is timely and, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Which of Wang, Mehl, Yokoyama or Chin should accompany Schultz.
Whether Schultz's priority is considered cleanly separable from Wang's role as his student and postdoc.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Car-Parrinello method made first-principles molecular dynamics practical by treating electronic and nuclear motion together, and it has changed how chemical reactions, liquids, interfaces and condensed phases are simulated from quantum mechanics. From my own field I can say its influence on enzyme and solution simulation is large. It is a clear and original method with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper is by exactly two people, which gives a clean and uncontroversial attribution. Whether Parrinello's later contributions (metadynamics, B058) count toward the same recognition is a separate matter, but the credited pair for this discovery is unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use, and it is routine in materials and chemistry research. Recognition has not been premature. Some argue it fits Physics rather than Chemistry, but its reach in chemistry is evident.
uncertainties: Computational methods were recognised recently (2013, 2024), which could lower the priority of another simulation prize.
The prize may be seen as belonging to physics; I cannot confirm the committee's view of that.
Parrinello's work is split across B053, B058 and B064, which complicates a single clean citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar-cell efficiencies from a few percent to above 25 percent in a decade, using solution-processed, simple materials. It is a new class of semiconductor with real device consequences and is among the most striking developments in energy chemistry. The simplicity and speed of its impact fit my game-changer criterion.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka (with Kojima) first used perovskites as sensitizers in 2009. Snaith's work on meso-superstructured cells and Park's solid-state cell with a stable high-efficiency device were decisive, and Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also contributed. Kojima is not among the credited names, which is an attribution gap because he was the first author of the original paper. The attribution is difficult.
assessment.maturity: The efficiency record is confirmed independently by many laboratories. Long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercialisation are unresolved, so recognition may be premature compared with candidates with deployed products.
uncertainties: Stability and commercial viability remain open, so a prize may be early.
Kojima's absence from the credited list and the crowded attribution make a fair three-person split hard.
I am recalling the early history from memory and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory and the funnel picture resolved Levinthal's paradox and gave a quantitative framework linking sequence, energetics and folding kinetics, which connect directly to experiment. As a theorist who values models that meet measurement, I find it conceptually important. Its impact on the field of protein folding and on structure prediction is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes, Onuchic and Bryngelson established the funnel concept and the principle of minimal frustration. Dill contributed the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model foundations, and Fersht the experimental mapping of folding pathways. The credit is spread across theory and experiment, which makes a three-person division contestable.
assessment.maturity: The theory has been tested by many experiments and simulations for three decades. The 2024 prize on structure prediction partly overlaps in subject, which could make this recognition either complementary or redundant.
uncertainties: Whether Fersht's experimental contribution should replace one of the theorists.
The overlap with the 2024 prize on protein structure may reduce urgency.
Concepts have been refined, so the exact claim to be credited is not crisp.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminator chemistry and single-molecule clusters made DNA sequencing cheap and fast enough to transform genomics and medicine. The chemistry, with reversible terminators and engineered polymerases, is the core innovation. The consequences are enormous.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa approach. Rothberg (pyrosequencing, 454) and Mayer, Ju and others made parallel contributions to alternative technologies, so credit for next-generation sequencing as a whole is spread widely. A prize limited to the Solexa chemistry is defensible but excludes other pioneers.
assessment.maturity: The technology is mature and ubiquitous. The recognition risk is that the prize is arguably more physiology or medicine or an overlap with Sanger's 1980 sequencing prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to credit a single platform among competing technologies.
Fit with Chemistry as against Medicine.
Priority disputes among Solexa, 454 and Lynx/Mayer.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles made it possible to deliver siRNA and mRNA into cells, and they were the enabling chemistry of the mRNA vaccines and the first siRNA drug. The consequences are very large and already real. The achievement is the chemistry and formulation, such as lipid pKa tuning and microfluidic mixing.
assessment.attribution: Cullis led the Vancouver work on lipid nanoparticle systems and ionizable lipids. Hope, Madden and MacLachlan contributed key formulation and ionizable lipid development, while Anderson and Langer supplied separate lipid libraries and delivery concepts. The attribution is hard to pin down given the many contributors and industry involvement, and the 2023 Medicine Prize went to the mRNA science, not delivery.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale, so the confirmation is strong. Recognition is timely, but attribution is difficult.
uncertainties: Who made the decisive ionizable-lipid advance, which I am recalling from memory and could not verify.
Industrial and patent history may blur academic priority.
Possible overlap with a recognition for the mRNA field.
